Olivia (support): escalation - customer hitting intermittent 502/504 and 'SSL connect error' on hosted /v1/generate since ~2026-03-15T08:10Z. They attached curl outputs and X-Request-Ids. Root TS: 1832001111
Raj (netops): We got edge-proxy alerts from eu-west around 08:09-08:18. High rate of TLS handshake timeouts and DNS "no such host" from our resolver pool. Noted a scheduled cert rollover last night; possible simultaneous DNS churn.
Kai (runtime): Repro from our synthetic: some sessions send ClientHello and never get ServerHello. Proxy logs:
```
[08:12:07] edge-eu-west proxy: tls handshake timeout to upstream customer-api.redwood-hosted.net
[08:12:07] dns-resolver-3: lookup customer-api.redwood-hosted.net -> temporary failure
[08:12:10] proxy: returning 502 to client after handshake failure
```
Maya (eng-sre): Customer provided pcap showing ServerHello absent during failed attempts. Their domain resolves via a CNAME to a third-party CDN, and DNS TTLs were set to 20s. CDN rotated certs ~08:05 and pushed a fast CNAME flip. Sequence looks like: cert rotate -> CDN updates -> resolvers see inconsistent mappings -> edge tries old cert target -> handshake fails.
Jess (customer): We triggered a CDN cert renew at 08:04 and briefly enabled a new origin mapping for testing. Errors started immediately. Curl from two EU exits:
```
curl -v https://customer-api.redwood-hosted.net/v1/generate
* TLS handshake times out
* SSL connect error
```
Olivia (support): Collected request ids and timelines. Customer traffic peaked ~300rps. Asking netops for immediate mitigations.
Raj (netops): Mitigations applied: 1) enabled multi-resolver fallback on affected edge nodes (added public resolvers), 2) flushed DNS cache on those nodes, 3) temporarily extended TLS handshake timeout from 3s -> 6s for a 15m canary. Rolling now.
Kai (runtime): Also wired emergency fallback to route to a compatible model variant if upstream fails, which reduces visible 5xxs while preserving responses albeit with slight perf hit. After changes we see handshake timeouts drop and 502 rate fall by ~70% in metrics.
Maya (eng-sre): Customer verified partial recovery after our changes. Full normalization once they rolled back the CDN mapping at ~08:25. Recommend documenting and automating detection for: simultaneous short-TTL CNAME swaps + cert rotations -> trigger protective mode (multi-resolver + bump handshake + route fallbacks).
Steve (billing): Customer asked about downtime credit. Support: capture full impact window and request-id list; we'll evaluate SLA credit once RCA done.
Jess (customer): Service stable now, thanks. Please follow up with final RCA and recommended configuration for minimal disruption during cert rollouts.
Olivia (support): Filing incident ticket with logs, pcmaps, request ids, and timeline. Assigning to eng-sre & netops for RCA. Actions recorded: dns flush, resolver fallback, handshake timeout canary, emergency route. Will update billing ticket. :white_check_mark:
Maya (eng-sre): RCA action items: - correlate CDN cert change window with our resolver failures - add alert for resolver ENOTFOUND spike + tls handshake timeouts - produce runbook for support to follow when customers use external CDNs during cert ops
Raj (netops): Also plan to add periodic resolver diversity in eu-west to avoid single-provider flaps and to implement faster cache invalidation hooks for emergency flushes.
Olivia (support): closing thread for now, will attach incident ID and link to RCA when ready. Thanks everyone.
